llm.summary: The package is internally consistent with its stated purpose (a macOS CLI that reads your browser session to manage Startup School, submit applications, and automate form fills), but it performs a few intrusive local actions (symlink creation and in-place patches) you should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name and description match the code and install: a Node CLI (yc) that reads Chrome cookies to access Startup School, calls Speedrun APIs, and uses Playwright to fill SPC Airtable forms. macOS restriction is explained by Keychain/Chrome cookie access. Required binary (yc) and node package are proportionate to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and source instruct the tool to read browser cookies (startupschool.org and account.ycombinator.com), fetch CSRF tokens from the dashboard page, call GraphQL/REST endpoints, and optionally drive Playwright to submit Airtable forms. Those operations are within scope, but note the tool auto-discovers all Chrome profiles and suggests clicking 'Always Allow' for Keychain access — it reads local profile metadata and cookie stores (expected for this use).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install uses an npm package (@lucasygu/yc-cli) from the public registry (package-lock shows registry.npmjs.org), which is a common pattern. The package runs a postinstall script that: (a) creates a symlink under ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli to register itself as a Claude/agent skill, and (b) patches files in node_modules/@steipete/sweet-cookie to work around local library bugs. Automated patching of node_modules and creating user-targeted symlinks are potentially intrusive but are performed locally and documented in the scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. The package needs read access to browser cookie stores and macOS Keychain decryption (to obtain session cookies), which is necessary to act on behalf of a logged-in Startup School user. It does scan Chrome Local State to find profiles (reads profile names), which is consistent with cookie discovery.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The postinstall script creates a persistent symlink under ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli so the package becomes available to the Claude Code/agent environment; preuninstall removes it if it points to this package. This is persistent agent-registration behavior (not an 'always: true' privilege), and it's explicit in the postinstall script, but it does modify user configuration directories automatically during install.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- This CLI needs to read your Chrome cookies and will prompt macOS Keychain requests; only install if you trust the package and want the CLI to act as your logged-in Startup School user.
- The npm postinstall will create ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli (registering the package as a Claude/agent skill) and will attempt in-place patches to a third-party module in node_modules; these are local filesystem modifications run automatically on install. If you prefer, run the package in an isolated environment or inspect the postinstall script before running.
- Playwright is a dependency and may download browser binaries when used; that is expected for form automation.
- If you want extra caution: review the upstream GitHub repo (SKILL.md includes https://github.com/lucasygu/yc-cli), audit the package contents, run npm install in a throwaway/macOS VM or container, or install without running postinstall (or manually create the ~/.claude symlink after review).
- If you do not want the package to auto-register as a Claude skill, do not allow the postinstall symlink — you can create the symlink manually after verifying the files, or edit/remove the postinstall step prior to installation.
